meta.name: Chemistry, Materials & Earth
meta.description: Chemistry institutes, advanced materials centers, climate & atmospheric observatories, oceanography hubs, milestones, and taxonomy.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

hubs.name: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
hubs.summary: Historic physical chemistry institute in Berlin-Dahlem leading heterogeneous catalysis, ultrafast surface physics, ab-initio electronic structure theory (FHI-aims), and cold-molecule spectroscopy.
hubs.nobel: Nobel laureates include Gerhard Ertl (2007 Chemistry, surface catalysis), Ernst Ruska (1986 Physics, electron microscope), Max von Laue, and Fritz Haber.

stages.postdoc: Max Planck and Alexander von Humboldt Postdoctoral Fellowships in green catalysis and ultrafast lasers.
stages.assoc_prof: Independent Research Group Leader awards advancing CO2-to-fuel electrochemistry.

hubs.name: Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung
hubs.summary: Despite its historic 1912 name ('Coal Research'), today one of the world's premier pure catalysis institutes—birthplace of Fischer-Tropsch chemistry, Ziegler-Natta polymerization, and Nobel-winning asymmetric organocatalysis.
hubs.nobel: Karl Ziegler (1963 Chemistry Nobel, polyethylene catalysis) and Benjamin List (2021 Chemistry Nobel, asymmetric organocatalysis).

hubs.name: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
hubs.summary: Global center for soft-matter physics and synthetic macromolecules—pioneering bottom-up graphene nanoribbons, organic electronics, multiscale molecular simulations, and bio-inspired smart polymers.

hubs.name: ICIQ (Institute of Chemical Research of Catalonia)
hubs.summary: Europe's dynamic catalysis research institute on Spain's Mediterranean coast—pioneering asymmetric homogeneous catalysis, photoredox synthesis, artificial photosynthesis solar fuels, and automated high-throughput screening.

hubs.name: UC Berkeley College of Chemistry
hubs.summary: Historic chemistry powerhouse where 16 periodic-table elements were discovered alongside Gilbert Lewis's covalent bond—today leading reticular MOF chemistry (Omar Yaghi), CRISPR biochemistry, and bioorthogonal synthesis.

hubs.name: ETH Zurich Department of Chemistry & Applied Biosciences (D-CHAB)
hubs.summary: One of Europe's foremost chemistry departments on ETH's Hönggerberg campus—advancing heterogeneous CO2 catalysis, synthetic organic methodology, microfluidic flow chemistry, and chemical biology.
hubs.nobel: Home to Chemistry Nobel laureates Vladimir Prelog, Leopold Ružička, Richard Ernst, Kurt Wüthrich, and Richard Kuhn.

hubs.name: ISIS (Institute of Supramolecular Science & Engineering, Strasbourg)
hubs.summary: Founded by Nobel laureate Jean-Marie Lehn at the University of Strasbourg—global epicenter of supramolecular chemistry, dynamic combinatorial libraries, polaritonic cavity chemistry, and molecular self-assembly.
hubs.nobel: Founded by Jean-Marie Lehn (1987 Chemistry Nobel); Strasbourg chemistry also honors Jean-Pierre Sauvage (2016 Nobel) and Martin Karplus (2013 Nobel).

hubs.name: Leibniz Institute for Catalysis (LIKAT)
hubs.summary: Europe's largest publicly funded applied catalysis institute—pioneering earth-abundant iron and manganese catalysts (Matthias Beller), green hydrogen storage in formic acid, and catalytic CO2 valorization into industrial feedstocks.

hubs.name: Kyoto University Institute for Chemical Research (ICR)
hubs.summary: Nearly century-old Kyoto University chemical powerhouse on the Uji campus—leading precision organometallic catalysis, synthetic carbon nanobelts, perovskite photovoltaics, and chemical bioinformatics (KEGG database).

hubs.name: National Graphene Institute (University of Manchester)
hubs.summary: Purpose-built cleanroom institute at the University of Manchester where graphene was first isolated in 2004—pioneering van der Waals 2D heterostructures, atomic-scale water desalination membranes, and graphene composites.
hubs.nobel: Home to Sir Andre Geim and Sir Konstantin Novoselov, winners of the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for isolating two-dimensional graphene.

projects.name: 2D van der Waals Heterostructures & Graphene Membranes

hubs.name: International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN, Northwestern)
hubs.summary: The first and largest dedicated nanotechnology institute in the US—pioneering spherical nucleic acids (Chad Mirkin), artificial molecular machines, dip-pen nanolithography, and ultraporous MOFs for gas storage and catalysis.
hubs.nobel: Sir J. Fraser Stoddart won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry at Northwestern for designing and synthesizing molecular machines.

hubs.name: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research (FKF)
hubs.summary: Premier European center bridging solid-state chemistry and nanoscale materials—advancing ionic transport in solid-state batteries (Joachim Maier), 2D layered oxides and nitrides, and high-pressure hydride superconductors.
hubs.nobel: Director Emeritus Klaus von Klitzing won the 1985 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the quantized Hall effect.

hubs.name: Argonne National Laboratory — Energy Storage & JCESR
hubs.summary: America's premier battery-materials national lab—inventor of the NMC lithium-ion cathode powering modern electric vehicles and leader of the Joint Center for Energy Storage Research (JCESR) advancing multivalent, solid-state, and flow batteries.

hubs.name: The Faraday Institution
hubs.summary: The UK's independent flagship institute for electrochemical energy storage—uniting 500+ researchers across 25+ universities to crack solid-state lithium dendrites, sodium-ion batteries, lithium-sulfur cells, and circular battery recycling.

hubs.name: Helmholtz Institute Ulm (HIU) for Electrochemical Energy Storage
hubs.summary: Joint battery-research center of KIT, Ulm University, DLR, and ZSW forming Germany's POLiS Cluster of Excellence—pioneering post-lithium sodium, magnesium, calcium, and chloride-ion battery chemistries.

hubs.name: CIC energiGUNE (Basque Energy Storage Research Center)
hubs.summary: Europe's leading electrochemical and thermal energy storage center in the Basque Country—combining solid-state polymer and ceramic battery prototyping, sodium-ion electrodes, and high-temperature thermal storage materials.

hubs.name: Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences (Göttingen)
hubs.summary: Formed from the legendary MPI for Biophysical Chemistry—epicenter of STED/MINFLUX nanoscopy (Stefan Hell), biomolecular molecular dynamics (GROMACS), ultrafast electron diffraction, and atomic cryo-EM.
hubs.nobel: Home to Stefan Hell (2014 Chemistry Nobel), Erwin Neher (1991 Medicine Nobel), and Manfred Eigen (1967 Chemistry Nobel, fast chemical reactions).

hubs.name: CECAM (European Centre for Atomic and Molecular Calculations)
hubs.summary: Europe's premier nexus for computational chemistry, atomistic simulation, and materials modeling—headquartered at EPFL with 17 European nodes convening global workshops on ab-initio molecular dynamics, enhanced sampling, and ML interatomic potentials.

hubs.name: Molecular Sciences Software Institute (MolSSI)

hubs.name: ETH Zurich Laboratory of Physical Chemistry (LPC)

hubs.name: RIKEN Theoretical Molecular Science & Computational Chemistry
hubs.summary: Japan's hub for ab-initio quantum chemistry, large-scale biomolecular simulation (GENESIS on the Fugaku supercomputer), and excited-state photochemistry—bridging relativistic electron-correlation theory with cellular crowding dynamics.

events.title: Lavoisier's Conservation of Mass & Modern Chemistry
events.summary: Overthrew phlogiston theory in Traité Élémentaire de Chimie, demonstrating oxygen's role in combustion, defining chemical elements, and proving mass is strictly conserved in chemical reactions.
events.impact: Transformed chemistry from qualitative alchemy into a rigorous quantitative physical science.

events.title: Alessandro Volta Invents the Voltaic Pile (First Electric Battery)
events.summary: Stacked alternating zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked cloth to generate the world's first continuous, steady electric current from chemical redox reactions.
events.impact: Launched electrochemistry (immediately enabling electrolysis of water and isolation of sodium and potassium) and made Oersted's and Faraday's electromagnetism experiments possible.

events.title: Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Table of the Elements
events.summary: Arranged chemical elements by atomic weight and recurring valence properties, boldly leaving gaps to predict the exact atomic weights and densities of undiscovered elements (gallium, scandium, germanium).
events.impact: Provided chemistry's master map and later revealed the quantum-mechanical shell structure of electrons.

events.title: The Keeling Curve Begins Continuous Atmospheric CO2 Tracking
events.summary: Installed precision infrared gas analyzers atop Mauna Loa (from Scripps Institution of Oceanography), recording both the biosphere's annual breathing cycle and the relentless rise of atmospheric CO2 from 315 ppm past 425 ppm.
events.impact: Became the foundational empirical record of modern climate science and anthropogenic greenhouse forcing.

events.title: First Quantitative Radiative-Convective Climate Model (CO2 Sensitivity)
events.summary: Simulated vertical radiative transfer, water-vapor feedback, and atmospheric convection on early digital computers, proving that doubling atmospheric CO2 warms Earth's surface by ~2°C while cooling the stratosphere.
events.impact: Established physical climate modeling and earned Syukuro Manabe half of the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: Invention of the Rechargeable Lithium-Ion Battery
events.figure: John B. Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham & Akira Yoshino
events.summary: John Goodenough discovered the high-voltage layered lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2) intercalation cathode at Oxford in 1980, paired by Akira Yoshino with a safe carbonaceous anode for Sony's 1991 commercialization.
events.impact: Unleashed lightweight rechargeable energy storage powering smartphones, laptops, electric vehicles, and grid-scale renewable batteries (2019 Chemistry Nobel).

events.title: Discovery of the Antarctic Ozone Hole & Montreal Protocol
events.figure: Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner & Jonathan Shanklin (BAS)
events.summary: British Antarctic Survey atmospheric scientists published decades of Dobson spectrophotometer measurements revealing catastrophic springtime stratospheric ozone depletion caused by human-made CFCs.
events.impact: Triggered the 1987 Montreal Protocol—the most successful international environmental treaty in history—setting the ozone layer on track to recover.

events.title: Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) & Reticular Chemistry
events.figure: Omar M. Yaghi, Susumu Kitagawa & Richard Robson
events.location: Tempe, AZ, Berkeley, CA & Kyoto, Japan
events.summary: Engineered crystalline porous coordination frameworks (such as MOF-5) by stitching metal-oxide clusters with organic linkers—achieving internal surface areas exceeding 7,000 m² per gram.
events.impact: Opened programmable molecular sponges for direct-air CO2 capture, desert atmospheric water harvesting, hydrogen storage, and clean catalysis.

trails.title: How Particle Physics Accidentally Built Open AI
trails.tagline: Trace the open-science lineage from CERN's Web invention and silica glass fibers to arXiv and Hugging Face.

stops.title: CERN
stops.bridge: To stop particle physicists from losing documentation across global universities, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 and released it royalty-free.

stops.title: MIT CSAIL
stops.bridge: Berners-Lee moved from Geneva to MIT to found the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), standardizing open protocols carried globally by glass optical fibers.

stops.title: Corning Sullivan Park Research
stops.bridge: Corning's 1970 invention of low-loss fused-silica optical fiber built the transoceanic laser highways enabling instant global scientific preprint sharing.

stops.title: Cornell Bowers CIS & arXiv
stops.bridge: Physicist Paul Ginsparg's arXiv server (stewarded at Cornell) turned instant open preprints into the heartbeat of physics, mathematics, and machine learning.

stops.title: Hugging Face
stops.bridge: Extended arXiv's open-paper culture to open model weights, code, and datasets—empowering labs worldwide to inspect and reproduce frontier AI.

stops.title: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)
stops.bridge: Completes the open-science stack by publishing Semantic Scholar's literature graph alongside fully open OLMo models, training corpora, and evaluation code.

trails.title: From Abyssal Seafloor Vents to Alien Ocean Worlds
trails.tagline: Discover how mapping Earth's hidden ocean floor transformed our search for extraterrestrial life and cosmic waves.

stops.title: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
stops.bridge: Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen drew the first global ocean-floor maps here, exposing the 40,000-mile mid-ocean volcanic ridge that proved plate tectonics.

stops.title: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
stops.bridge: Diving down to those volcanic ridges in submersible Alvin in 1977, WHOI discovered sunless chemosynthetic life thriving on hydrothermal vents.

stops.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography
stops.bridge: Expanded global ocean-atmosphere sensing via the Keeling Curve and 4,000 autonomous Argo floats—honing remote sensing for icy planetary oceans.

stops.title: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
stops.bridge: Directly inspired by Earth's hydrothermal vents, JPL engineered Europa Clipper to probe Jupiter's moon for a warm, life-supporting subsurface saltwater ocean.

stops.title: ESA ESTEC
stops.bridge: Europe's technical space hub launched Juice toward Jupiter's icy moons and is now engineering the 2.5-million-km LISA laser interferometer in space.

stops.title: LIGO Observatory
stops.bridge: Proved gravitational-wave interferometry on Earth—paving the way for ESA/NASA's space-borne LISA to hear supermassive black holes collide across cosmic time.

trails.title: Catalysts, Fusion Magnets & AI Weather Twins for Earth
trails.tagline: How atomic materials discovery, burning-plasma magnets, and AI climate models unite to safeguard a habitable planet.

stops.title: Fritz Haber Institute (Berlin)
stops.bridge: Decoded the atomic surface physics of catalysis and built NOMAD open materials repositories to accelerate zero-carbon chemical reactions.

stops.title: Molecular Foundry & Materials Project (LBNL)
stops.bridge: Published 150,000+ computed crystal structures openly online, powering AI crystal-discovery engines and autonomous robotic synthesis labs.

stops.title: MIT Chemistry & Materials Science
stops.bridge: Advanced high-temperature REBCO superconducting tapes and solid-state batteries—unlocking compact, ultra-high-field magnets for clean fusion.

stops.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS)
stops.bridge: Spun out of MIT to assemble the SPARC compact net-energy tokamak using 20-tesla REBCO magnets aimed at commercial zero-carbon baseload energy.

stops.title: ECMWF (Weather & Climate AI)
stops.bridge: While fusion tackles future emissions, ECMWF's ERA5 reanalysis and AIFS/GraphCast AI models sharpen extreme-weather warnings days further ahead.

stops.title: British Antarctic Survey
stops.bridge: Having discovered the 1985 Ozone Hole, BAS now tracks West Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier to bound future global sea-level rise.

stops.title: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
stops.bridge: Synthesizes polar ice, ocean circulation, and energy models into Earth's Planetary Boundaries and climate tipping-point guardrails.

trails.title: Decoding Life: From Heredity to Genomic AI
trails.tagline: Follow DNA from its discovery as genetic code through million-fold sequencing drops, CRISPR, and 40B-parameter genome models.

stops.title: The Rockefeller University
stops.bridge: In 1944, Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty proved here that DNA—not protein—is the molecule carrying genetic heredity.

stops.title: Wellcome Sanger Institute
stops.bridge: Using Frederick Sanger's chain-termination sequencing, decoded one-third of the Human Genome Project and established open global genomic data.

stops.title: Cambridge Dept. of Chemistry
stops.bridge: Just up the road, Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis—slashing whole-genome costs from $100M to under $200.

stops.title: Innovative Genomics Institute (CRISPR)
stops.bridge: Once biology could read genomes cheaply, Jennifer Doudna's CRISPR-Cas9 gave humanity the molecular word processor to edit DNA precisely.

stops.title: Arc Institute (Palo Alto)
stops.bridge: Now trains 40B-parameter genomic foundation models (Evo 2) across 9.3 trillion DNA bases to design novel genetic circuits and Virtual Cells.

stops.title: AHRI & KRISP (Durban)
stops.bridge: Brings high-speed genomics to global public health—tracking emerging viral variants in real time across Africa to protect the entire world.

trails.title: Catalysts, 2D Materials & the Solid-State Battery Race
trails.tagline: See how atomic surface catalysis, nanographenes, and AI crystal labs converge to power zero-carbon energy storage.

stops.title: Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung
stops.bridge: From Karl Ziegler's polymer catalysts to Benjamin List's Nobel asymmetric organocatalysis, revealed how atomically tailored active sites steer chemical reactions with minimal waste.

stops.title: Fritz Haber Institute (Berlin)
stops.bridge: Gerhard Ertl's atomic surface-science spectroscopy imaged catalytic reactions directly on metal crystals, establishing the blueprint for clean electrocatalysis.

stops.title: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
stops.bridge: Bottom-up organic synthesis produces atomically precise nanographenes, 2D conductive frameworks, and ion-transporting polymer membranes.

stops.title: Cambridge Dept. of Chemistry
stops.bridge: Clare Grey's operando solid-state NMR peers inside working lithium and sodium batteries in real time to diagnose and prevent deadly dendrite growth.

stops.title: The Molecular Foundry & Materials Project (LBNL)
stops.bridge: Combines 150,000+ openly computed crystal structures with A-Lab robotic synthesis to accelerate discovery of cobalt-free cathodes and solid-state electrolytes.

stops.title: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL)
stops.bridge: Integrates next-generation battery cells with >33%-efficient perovskite-silicon tandem solar modules and megawatt grid testbeds to decarbonize global power.

trails.title: Listening to Earth: Ice Cores, Oceans & Satellites
trails.tagline: Connect polar ice-core time capsules, abyssal ocean floats, and exascale AI climate digital twins monitoring our living planet.

stops.title: British Antarctic Survey
stops.bridge: After exposing the 1985 Ozone Hole, BAS ice-core and Thwaites Glacier expeditions unlocked 800,000 years of trapped ancient atmosphere and sea-level projections.

stops.title: Alfred Wegener Institute (AWI)
stops.bridge: Operates icebreaker RV Polarstern and leads the Beyond EPICA campaign drilling 1.5-million-year-old Antarctic ice to decode Earth's ancient glacial rhythm.

stops.title: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
stops.bridge: Deploys deep-sea moorings, autonomous gliders, and submersible Alvin to track how Earth's oceans absorb over 90% of excess planetary heat and drive Atlantic circulation.

stops.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography
stops.bridge: Maintains the continuous Keeling Curve Mauna Loa CO2 record alongside the 4,000-float global Argo array profiling ocean temperature and salinity worldwide.

stops.title: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research
stops.bridge: Fuses polar, oceanic, and atmospheric observations inside the open Community Earth System Model (CESM) to simulate centuries of coupled climate physics.

stops.title: ECMWF (Weather & Climate AI)
stops.bridge: Assimilates hundreds of millions of daily satellite measurements into ERA5 reanalysis and AIFS machine-learning weather models for life-saving global forecasts.
